questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was very important to me that Uppsala was a very student friendly city especially the 'sorority' houses and the nice cafées was a big part of my experience.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I thought it was really hard to take courses that is not in my field of study. The exams were difficult because of the formalities - but it was good to try something very different.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Uppsala campus is really big, but it did not feel so big at any time. There was a nice introduction and a tour upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to get my student id, and the reception was very helpfull. Maybe they are used to mecenat app, so they thought it was very sweet that i wanted a campus card.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was okay. I lived at a 'dorm' outside of Uppsala. It was fine to take the train.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of options, at one point you just have to pick something.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: i dont know since i knew where is was going to live

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. Much like in Denmark

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Students and Erasmus

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got some of the classes i wanted, but i would have liked to have attended some of the ethnology classes i applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pick the destination and the student environment first, and then the classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some of the grammar heavy classes where to much for me as a non native speaker...

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: BA level 'Nordiska Språk'

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: All of my teachers were really nice, but more distanced from the class that i am used to. But to be fair, that might have reflected more on the students attendance. We did not really get to know the professors that much (except for Lisa Hansen, a danish professor that helped me a lot during my exams and frustrations)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Isländska, Språkstruktur,  Svenskan i tid och rum, Dansk/Norsk  (30ects)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Svenskan i tid och rum and Dansk/Norsk, if you are coming from a nordic country. The Isländska, Språkstruktur was too difficult to follow as a foreigner

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Books were cheaper, but if you buy second hand like i did, make sure to have cash if you dont have Swish

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I actually had a lot to do in my free time, so i spend a lot of time in the library, cafées, in the park ect. I really wanted to join a choir, but i missed the audition date

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots. The 'sorority houses' hosts a lot of events. I have been to several dance nights at V-dalarna on Eptu.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Make sure to sign up for choir!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hang at the 'sorority' bars and drink coffee.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I love Sweden.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Swedes are in my opinion either very shy or very outgoing (mostly in groups), much like the danes. So just be yourself and try to ask some questions for example when working in groups.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The language and the costs of everything :)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Bring warm clothes, get in a 'sorority' and spot the nice cafées (Uno, Queen beans)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to speak swedish - they do not understand danish :-)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: There is a lot to choose from. But it really felt like the world was opening up to me - in a different way than if you are traveling or visiting.. living in another country by yourself gives you some chest hair

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Exams. Without a doubt. They where different, and much more old fashioned than i am used to. Sitting four hours with nothing but a piece of paper and your water bottle is very different from writing at home/library/etc over several weeks.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It was great.. but i failed two of my courses, and i had not failed anything before that.. so that was a tough thing to experience for the first time, and also feeling like you took someones money for granted..

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
